raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation Currently, the entire AITER attention code path has a `torch.compile.disable` decorator, introduced in #20319 . This is only required for the FP8 path, not BF16. This hurts the performance of some models (such as FLUX) a lot. This PR limits the scope of that decorator. PR #21431 added support for MXFP4 quantization and for skipping the quantization for certain layers (`--quantization-ignored-layers`). The MXFP4 implementation was not torch.compile compatible, so only way to use it with compile enabled was to add a `torch.compile.disable` decorator. This PR wraps the quantization in a custom op that is opaque to the compiler, allowing it to be compiled correctly. Also wires in the ignored layers that weren't properly used before. ## Modifications 1. Limit the `torch.compile.disable` decorator only to the FP8 path, instead of the full AITER implementation. 2. Create a custom op for the MXFP4 operations, making it torch.compile compatible. 3. Wire in the `--quantization-ignored-layers` values to the quantization layers. ## Accuracy Tests FLUX2 quantization output with/without compile enabled: FLUX1 comparison before/after AITER fix: ## Speed Tests and Profiling FLUX perf gain after the AITER fix: ``` #### 1. Mxfp4LinearMethod.apply dropped the is_gfx95_supported() check, so on NVIDIA (and any non-gfx95 platform) it no longer raises RuntimeError: MXFP4 inference requires ROCm and MI350+ and instead calls the unregistered torch.ops.sglang.mxfp4_diffusion_quant_gemm; please restore that guard before the op call.

There's a check in the `process_weights_after_loading` for GFX950, which is called in standard usage before the `apply`, so that would catch this. In cases where it's called directly without the loading part, like possibly in unit tests, the guard would not fire.

Applying the guard in `apply` causes a graph break mid run, as it has to call torch internals for the GFX950 check, so I would rather keep it away from there. I moved the gfx check from `process_weights_after_loading` to `__init__`, so both usage and direct usages are guarded.

What do you think, is this good?
Yes. __init__ is the right place: it runs for both the load path and a direct apply, and it stays outside the compiled graph. Resolving this comment.

   Why: The signature check runs for every --quantization method on every backend, including NVIDIA and non-gfx95 AMD, and forwards ignored_layers with no platform condition.
   Fix: Run the signature check and ignored_layers assignment only under is_gfx95_supported(), and leave every other backend on the previous method set.
Reverted the change and updated the tests to match.
